title: U.S. House · California's 16th Congressional District
area: Santa Clara County, centered on San Jose.

context.text: This district's boundaries changed under California Proposition 50, the mid-decade congressional redistricting measure voters approved in November 2025. Incumbent Sam Liccardo and Republican Peter Soule advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, defeating Kevin Johnson and Jotham Stein.

candidates.name: Sam Liccardo
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with about 76% of the vote.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for California's 16th Congressional District (since 2025); previously Mayor of San Jose (2015-2023)

summary.text: Sam Liccardo is the Democratic incumbent representing California's 16th Congressional District, which runs from Half Moon Bay and Pacifica through Silicon Valley, including San Jose, Palo Alto and Mountain View. A former prosecutor, San Jose City Council member and two-term mayor of San Jose, he was first elected to Congress in 2024 and sits on the House Financial Services Committee. His campaign materials emphasize housing, lowering the cost of living, and bipartisan legislation.

background.text: Born April 16, 1970. According to his Ballotpedia survey, he grew up in the district; Ballotpedia lists Bellarmine College Preparatory as his high school.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Georgetown University (1991, per Ballotpedia), and a law degree (1996) and a master's degree in public policy from Harvard (Kennedy School) (1996).

Worked as a prosecutor of sexual assault and child exploitation crimes in the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office and as a federal prosecutor in the Southern District of California. In his Ballotpedia survey he also lists college professor among his past roles.
Elected to the San Jose City Council (District 3) in 2006 and served from 2007 to 2015; won re-election in 2010.

Elected mayor of San Jose in November 2014 and re-elected in 2018, serving two terms. His House website says San Jose committed to carbon neutrality, expanded community-based policing and launched a large rent relief program during his tenure.
Won the open U.S. House seat in November 2024, defeating fellow Democrat Evan Low, succeeding retiring Rep. Anna Eshoo; took office January 3, 2025.

Serves on the House Committee on Financial Services and chairs the New Democratic Coalition's Innovation & Technology Working Group; in July 2025 he led the New Dems' Innovation Agenda, according to his House website.
According to his House website, he and his wife, Jessica Garcia-Kohl, a nonprofit leader, live in Saratoga.

priorities.text: Campaign site lists making housing more affordable, reducing the cost of living, and protecting rights and democracy as his core priorities.
Launched "Innovation for Good" (I4G), an effort he describes as building a pragmatic, pro-innovation Democratic majority in Congress by leveraging technology to address national challenges.

positions.summary: Led or co-led four bills included in the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which his office describes as the most significant federal housing reform package in more than 30 years, including the BUILD Housing Act and the Unlocking Housing Supply Through Streamlined and Modernized Reviews Act.
In his Candidate Connection survey he says he cosponsored measures to eliminate tariffs and supported efforts to eliminate tariffs he describes as price-inflating.
positions.quote: I cosponsored measures to eliminate tariffs

positions.summary: In his Candidate Connection survey he says he will continue fighting to defend reproductive rights.
positions.quote: I will continue fighting to defend your reproductive rights and voting rights, and to protect funding for Social Security, MediCal, and CalFresh

positions.summary: In his Candidate Connection survey he says he introduced a bipartisan extension of the ACA tax credits and will work to protect Medi-Cal funding.
positions.quote: I introduced the only bipartisan ACA tax credit extension that lowers health premiums while saving taxpayer dollars

positions.summary: In his Candidate Connection survey he says he is leading legislation to incentivize renewables and batteries for data centers.
positions.quote: I am leading legislation to incentivize renewables and batteries for data centers

record.text: Authored the BUILD Housing Act, the Unlocking Housing Supply Through Streamlined and Modernized Reviews Act, the RESIDE Act, and the Property Improvement and Manufactured Housing Loan Modernization Act, all included in the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act that became law on July 13, 2026.
Introduced the bipartisan Payments Access and Consumer Efficiency (PACE) Act with Rep. Young Kim (R-CA) to modernize payment-processing access and reduce consumer fees.
Assigned to the House Committee on Financial Services in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Served on the San Jose City Council and as mayor of San Jose from 2015 to 2023.

candidates.name: Peter Soule
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with about 11% of the vote.

summary.text: Peter Soule is the Republican candidate for California's 16th Congressional District. According to his campaign website, he worked in his family's steel business, served on the San Jose Civil Service Commission from 2007 to 2011, and has been a Santa Clara County Republican volunteer and central committee member since 2004-2005. He is campaigning on public safety, reducing state regulation, lowering housing and energy costs, and immigration enforcement.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he holds a B.A. from UC Santa Barbara and an M.B.A. in Finance from Golden Gate University.

Worked in the family steel business, Soule Steel, in San Francisco and Los Angeles, which his campaign site says his grandfather founded in 1911. He lists roles in commercial property management, accounting and finance, and the architectural products division.
Served on the San Jose Civil Service Commission from 2007 to 2011.

Has volunteered in every election since 2004 for the Santa Clara County Republican Party and individual candidates, was Supervisorial District 4 leader for the Silicon Valley GOP in 2020, and has served on its central committee since 2005 as a member or alternate and as a California Republican Party delegate, according to his campaign website.

priorities.text: Says he will advocate for withholding federal funds from cities with sanctuary-city policies and for removing federal highway funds from states that issue commercial driver's licenses to people who cannot read English.

Says he will work to lower the cost of water for farmers by reforming the federal Endangered Species Act and increasing water storage capacity, and to make energy more affordable by easing restrictions on oil drilling and refineries in California.
Says he will work to reduce housing costs by banning large financial institutions from buying single-family homes and shielding Baby Boomers who sell homes from capital gains tax.

positions.summary: Says he will advocate for withholding federal dollars from cities that enforce sanctuary-city policies that prevent the deportation of people in the country illegally who commit crimes.
Says he will oppose local policies that limit Second Amendment rights.

statements.quote: Enact Federal policies to protect parental rights and enable parents to send their children to their school of choice.
statements.context: On his campaign website's issues page

statements.quote: Make energy more affordable by removing restrictions on drilling for oil and building refineries in California.
statements.context: On his campaign website's issues page

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and priorities from his campaign website's issues page (souleforcongress.com/issues). Two additional statements added. No questionnaire, debate or forum coverage found; the site does not address abortion, taxes, health care, tariffs or most other guide issues.
